question: Do sacrifice-bunt tries with nobody out gain win probability?
answer: No. Bunt tries cost 0.3 to 0.9 win-prob pts per try vs swinging; late and close, up to 1.9.
findings: Runner on 1st, 0 out: -0.3 pts (CI -0.4 to -0.1), n=5,068 tries of 107,555 PAs.
Runner on 2nd: -0.7 pts (CI -1.0 to -0.4). 1st and 2nd: -0.9 pts (CI -1.1 to -0.6).
1st and 2nd, 7th inning on, within 1 run: -1.9 pts (CI -2.8 to -1.0), n=700 tries.
Realized WE to end of inning: no CI excludes 0 (1st: -0.2 pts). Try rate 9.1% 2015, 6.5% 2025.
method: Non-pitcher PAs, 0 out, innings 1-9. Bunt try = bunt in play or foul/missed bunt. Outcome: change in empirical WE over the PA. OLS with batter and on-deck season wOBA, inning x score x season cells; SE clustered by game.
data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2015-2025 regular season, 158,989 PAs with runners on and 0 out, 9,669 bunt tries. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
split_check: PA-level loss in both eras for 2nd and 1st+2nd; runner on 1st: -0.5 pts 2015-19, -0.0 2020-25 (n.s.).
